admission.justification: The developer explicitly rejects child-inclusive compact marks/counts in favor of major-only progress plus hierarchical child disclosure, which constrains all later step-summary surfaces. The choice governs future authoring and consumers, not this leaf’s schedule.

alternatives.option: Use one progress/count unit per major step across tool and dashboard surfaces; keep child activity in the major display state and child detail in cached hover and the task list.
alternatives.reason: The developer explicitly rejects child-inclusive compact marks/counts in favor of major-only progress plus hierarchical child disclosure, which constrains all later step-summary surfaces.

alternatives.option: Flatten major steps and sub-steps into separate compact marks and counted progress units.
alternatives.reason: D283 explicitly calls showing each child as a task dot a mistake; it changes the visible denominator and obscures the requested hover hierarchy.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Only a new developer-approved progress-unit contract that deliberately counts children while retaining the distinction from canonical closeout readiness.

consequences: Major-only count and compact marks must agree across the tool response, sidebar, master row and task page.
Nested task-page detail remains available; hover adds no request or keyboard stop; bar rows do not acquire dot tooltips.
Child activity changes the unfinished major’s display state, not canonical state or closeout obligations.
context: The previous implementation gives 5 majors and 8 children 13 compact marks and a child-inclusive denominator, contrary to the developer’s intended task-level summary.
